tests.name: Effective description
tests.reasoning: The description uses imperative phrasing ('Use this skill when...'), focuses on user-facing symptoms ('an agent will not start or cannot be invoked', 'returns nothing or produces no traces', 'behaves differently in production than in test'), explicitly covers trigger contexts even when the user doesn't name the underlying domain terms ('even if they do not mention runtime roles, VPC endpoints, service control policies, OTLP telemetry or aliasing by name'), and remains concise at roughly 4 sentences.
tests.evidence: Use this skill when an agent will not start or cannot be invoked, when a gateway or action group fails, when an agent returns nothing or produces no traces, when it behaves differently in production than in test, or when someone asks which agent version is actually live, even if they do not mention runtime roles, VPC endpoints, service control policies, OTLP telemetry or aliasing by name.

tests.name: Verbosity and conciseness
tests.reasoning: The body avoids explaining general concepts (e.g., what IAM, VPC, or OTLP are) and goes straight into domain-specific procedures, check-ids, and AWS-specific API calls. The text is dense but every sentence conveys project-specific, non-obvious information the agent would not otherwise know.
tests.evidence: "Every finding is grounded in the catalogs under references/: checks-agentcore.md (LLM-AC-001..014...) and checks-agents.md (LLM-AGT-001..011...)"

tests.name: Detailed reference materials must not be in body
tests.reasoning: Detailed reference data (check catalogs, metric thresholds, API quirks) are kept in references/ files and the body only summarizes with pointers; the Router table is a navigation aid, not a data dump, and conditional branches link out to references/router-details.md rather than inlining detail.
tests.evidence: "How to read each API and metric is in references/collection-reference.md. Load it with any row."

tests.name: Reference files must be linked
tests.reasoning: Every file under references/ is linked with a markdown link somewhere in the body.
tests.evidence: "references/checks-agentcore.md (LLM-AC-001)" and "[`references/router-details.md`](references/router-details.md)" style links appear for all reference files.

tests.name: Reference links must specify when to load
tests.reasoning: Reference links are embedded in a Router table that ties each file to a specific triggering condition (e.g., runtime won't start, gateway target failing), clearly specifying when to load each.
tests.evidence: "AgentCore runtime will not start / cannot invoke | ... | references/checks-agentcore.md (LLM-AC-001)"

tests.name: Reference path format
tests.reasoning: All reference paths use relative paths of the form references/filename.md with no absolute paths or traversals.

tests.name: Prescription vs description
tests.reasoning: Fragile, order-dependent operations (the two review procedures) are given exact ordered steps with specific APIs and check-ids, while flexible areas like interpreting hypotheses or related skills guidance are described with reasoning and 'why' rather than rigid scripts.
tests.evidence: "Step 2: Simulate the runtime role with iam:SimulatePrincipalPolicy for every action it exercises..." contrasted with "List the likely causes as hypotheses, most likely first, each with the read-only check or isolation test that would confirm or rule it out"

tests.name: Defaults, not menus
tests.reasoning: Where migration paths or methods are offered, one is marked as the primary/closest analog and the others as alternatives rather than an undifferentiated list.
tests.evidence: "the two recommended migration paths are the AgentCore harness (config-based, the closest analog to Classic) or code-defined agents on AgentCore"

tests.name: Favor procedures over declarations
tests.reasoning: The two procedures teach a generalizable approach (steps to diagnose any runtime/agent) rather than a one-off instance; the Router table generalizes across many operator-reported symptoms.
tests.evidence: "Step 1: Read the runtime with bedrock-agent:ListAgentRuntimes / GetAgentRuntime — status, version, endpoint, and the execution role ARN" generalizes to any runtime, not a specific instance.

tests.name: Gotchas section
tests.reasoning: The skill has an extensive 'Common wrong answers' section and 'Error Handling' section documenting non-obvious pitfalls like alias vs DRAFT resolution and permission-denial false negatives, functioning as a gotchas section.
tests.evidence: "An agent's LIVE behaviour is its alias→version resolution, NOT the latest prepared DRAFT (api-quirks.md §6)."

tests.name: Templates and outputs missing
tests.reasoning: The skill produces structured findings/reports and provides an explicit template asset for this purpose.
tests.evidence: "assets/agent-runtime-report-template.md — consolidated review output (scope, findings with check-ids and severities, remediation, disclosed gaps)"

tests.name: Templates and outputs must not be in body
tests.reasoning: No large inline templates exist in the body; the only output template is referenced externally in assets/.
tests.evidence: "When a full report is requested, the output follows assets/agent-runtime-report-template.md."

tests.name: Asset files must be linked
tests.reasoning: The single asset file is referenced multiple times in the body.

tests.name: Asset links must specify when to load
tests.reasoning: The asset reference specifies the condition under which it should be used — when a full report is requested.
tests.evidence: "When a full report is requested, the output follows assets/agent-runtime-report-template.md."

tests.name: Asset path format
tests.reasoning: The asset reference uses a relative path format from the skill root.

tests.name: Step-by-step guidance
tests.reasoning: Both procedures (AgentCore review and Bedrock Agents Classic review) use the required checkbox checklist format with 'Step N:' labeling, satisfying the procedural requirement.
tests.evidence: "- [ ] Step 1: Read the runtime with bedrock-agent:ListAgentRuntimes / GetAgentRuntime..."

tests.name: Validation loops
tests.reasoning: The skill includes an explicit 'Before You Present — Validate Your Own Output' section instructing the agent to re-check its findings for evidence, correctness, and completeness before presenting.
tests.evidence: "Before you present an agent/runtime review, re-check your own output against this list. Treat it as a gate, not a suggestion."
